_comment: 🎨️ SVG 1.1/✳️tiny's own contribution to the repository test platform: `quick-xml` 0.42 registered as the independent reference reader/writer for THIS subset's own 10-kind `SvgTinyMutation` vocabulary, and the comparison profile that vocabulary is measured under. A distinct id and capability from the sibling `✳️any` and `✳️basic` registrations: a mutation vocabulary belongs to the subset that declares it, and reusing an approved oracle outside its surveyed capability fails the contract's oracle-capability-mismatch check.

oracles.rationale:
🩹️ RECLASSIFIED (ticket SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION, shard A10, 2026-09-02). This entry was registered `third-party-library` on the strength of a real crate that does genuine codec work, but the mutation's expected RESULT is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs` -- its dispatch function's catch-all arm is `"mutation kind {...} has no oracle implementation"`, proof that every OTHER arm is an implementation, not a reading. Both halves of the comparison then descend from the same specification, so a shared misreading produces two agreeing wrong answers -- the one failure a differential oracle exists to catch. This is a `cross-semio-implementation`: a required SUPPLEMENT (metamorphic/inverse/round-trip evidence), never a substitute. A qualifying third-party reference for the mutation semantics is still owed. See $TICKET/📓️a10-oracle-honesty.md.

quick-xml is a general streaming XML reader AND writer, not an SVG library and not a profile validator, which is what makes it usable as the independent producer here: this subset's oracle (../🦀️oracle.rs) builds its own element tree from quick-xml's event stream through the shared 📰markup family module, applies each declared SvgTinyMutation kind to that tree with independently written viewBox/transform grammars and its own transcription of REC-SVGMobile-20030114's excluded-element and excluded-attribute lists, and re-serializes with quick-xml's Writer. It never imports this repository's own xml_document_from_text/write_svg_xml codec, nor its check_svg_tiny_conformance. Both blocklists encode the same normative W3C list; neither is derived from the other, which is the point.

comparisonProfiles.description: SVG Tiny 1.1 mutation round trips compared structurally: element/text/CDATA/comment/PI tree shape and content exact, attributes compared as a name-sorted set (attribute order is real writer freedom), and the viewBox/transform attribute values decomposed into typed numeric geometry rather than compared as raw strings, with a small absolute tolerance for cross-implementation float formatting. Self-closing versus explicit empty open/close tags are equivalent by construction — both parse to zero children — and are never distinguished by either side. Nothing about the PROFILE is narrowed away: the presence or absence of an excluded element or a forbidden presentation attribute is exactly what the tree comparison sees, so strip-non-tiny and the gated authoring kinds are compared on the ground the profile is defined on.
